workflow.summary: High-evidence documents are extracted and audited in parallel; source-reviewed records then feed reusable material/method reader pages and separate training exports.
workflow.screening_scope: The fixed screening collection contains 10,802 distinct document contents in 10,967 source files. Main articles and SI are separate documents; exact duplicate contents are counted once in distinct-content rates. The initial screen is 99.074% complete, with 100 access-blocked items still unreviewed. New arrivals remain queued separately.
steps: Screen every fixed-cutoff document independently; preserve source copies, format holds and prior coverage. Missing companions do not block screening.
Rank measured/refined atomic-structure candidates with usable recipes first; keep phase, size and morphology-linked recipes as a separate useful tier.
Verify recipe–sample–structure evidence within each retained source, and verify source relationships when joining information from different documents.
Retain all screened candidates and gaps; external reference cells, simulations and molecular-precursor coordinates do not become measured product pairs.
Build and publish academic material readers only after the selected paper’s source, data, figure and independent audit gates pass.
workflow.capacity: The user requires at least 500 complete source-checked website contributions/day. Local Qwen3.5:9B measured 108–137 short-source first-pass drafts/hour; a separate 27B cross-check of the Tirosh draft took 32.09 s but missed a known 300 K / 230–300 °C conflict and had no rendered figures. This does not establish audited publication throughput. The original three-source reader pilot remains 0/3 integrated; no honest end-to-end daily rate or finish date is established. Continue local batching, evidence quotes/locators, independent source and figure checks, reusable page generation, and batched QA; count only audited, integrated, QA-passed contributions. Meeting 500/day at full standard requires a validated larger review pipeline and additional independent reviewer capacity; paid/API processing remains unapproved.
workflow.paid_processing: No paid API or cloud document processing is active; the user deferred the budget decision. Local RTX 5090/Qwen3.5 extraction and cross-model audit tests have run with cloud disabled; the distinct 27B audit still missed a known conflict. A page-wise quote-presence validator is now tested (14/16 quotes matched on one page) as a rejection filter, not a scientific audit. Source PDFs remain local; visual/source review and integration are still required.

workflow.update_policy: Progress is published at meaningful review milestones. Drafts and source-audit passes are not counted as website contributions; each published record must retain evidence locators and clear source/sample distinctions.

estimate.summary: Target: 500 fully audited, integrated, browser-validated source-paper contributions/day (20.83/hour continuously). The selected historical end-to-end cohort was 9 closures in 12.87 hours (0.70/hour; 16.8/day by arithmetic only, not a forecast), about 29.8 times below target. Current concurrency and local draft models do not demonstrate the target; no credible full-corpus finish date is available.
estimate.current_batch: Chen et al. (2018) status-only correction passed independent delta audit and local browser checks; public deployment/live check is pending. ACS Nano A1–A10 independent audit found two correction items. Rusch/Manna 2026 audit confirmed source quantities/tables checked so far but found 22/23 origin-pointer gaps plus material/page mapping defects. Tirosh, Wu and phosphinate-CdSe reader pilot remain tracked separately.
notes: Frozen pass set: 5,539 distinct source contents in 5,587 copied files (48 duplicates); main articles and SI are separate screen units, not unique-paper or recipe counts.
Screening pass indicates useful synthesis/preparation evidence plus structural, phase or morphology evidence; it is not an exact sample-pair, source audit or training admission.
Keep every source-reported condition, sample and recipe variant separate. Several papers can contribute independently cited details to one material page.

A small local Qwen3.5:9B benchmark processed two short main articles in 27.6–33.3 s each. It nevertheless missed key source conflicts and sample distinctions. Draft rate is not audited website throughput.

Local extraction drafts are not counted as reviewed website contributions. The Qwen3.5:27B benchmark exposed a conflict-normalization error and missing work-up/statistical details; every candidate still requires an independent source check.
The local model runs offline with cloud features disabled. No paid API or external document upload is authorized.
The local site renderer previously processed 680 records in 11.5 s; source reading, independent review, conflict handling and reader QA—not HTML generation—control end-to-end throughput.
A distinct 27B cross-check caught an omitted reagent but missed the Tirosh 300 K / 230–300 °C conflict and did not inspect figures; model-to-model agreement is not an audit.
Page-wise quote matching rejected two of 16 candidate spans from one Tirosh page; this is a filter test, not a completed paper or audited contribution.

500/day arithmetic: 20.83 completed papers/hour around the clock, or one every 2.88 minutes. Under the earlier 30–60 min per-paper review planning assumption this would require 250–500 reviewer-hours/day (31–63 eight-hour reviewers), before integration overhead; this is a planning bound, not measured labor.

daily_throughput.counting_rule: Count one source paper only after its scoped source reading, independent scientific audit, recipe/sample/figure checks, material-page integration and browser validation pass. Multiple recipe rows from one paper count once. Drafts and screening skips do not count as website papers built.

daily_throughput.capacity_note: The 500/day target requires 20.83 completed papers/hour continuously, one every 2.88 minutes. The current four-lane ceiling and measured end-to-end cohort do not demonstrate this. No paid API or external compute run is active.
